results.title: CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse
results.abstract: This paper presents CacheSmith, a KV cache reuse system for RAG prefill that maximizes quality-gated SLO attainment. While context caching lowers prefill latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks, it misses cross-chunk attention that a full prefill would compute over concatenated inputs. Prior selective recomputation schemes tackle this problem but enforce static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to effectively handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a three-phase workflow of WarmUp, Probe, and Patch that can be dynamically configured to exploit a wide range of cost-accuracy trade-offs. At serving time, an SLO-aware scheduler in CacheSmith forms batches to mitigate inter-request interference during layer-by-layer prefill, while a budget-aware planner configures recomputation phases across the batch to maximize the number of requests satisfying both generation quality and latency targets. Both components make fast, solver-free decisions over profiled cost-accuracy bands. On four benchmarks across varying arrival rates and burstiness levels, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%, over four state-of-the-art baselines.

results.title: Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels
results.abstract: Attention Matching (AM) compacts a KV cache by keeping some keys per head, refitting their values and adding a bias to each kept key's logit. FlashAttention and vLLM's paged caches have no input for it. We fold the bias into the keys along one closed-form direction per head, fitted on context queries, giving a plain cache with AM's size and head dimension and the model's own query path; the output error is bounded by how far each query's projection on that direction is from 1. With equal per-head budgets, unmodified vLLM serves folded caches through a KV connector, matching Hugging Face's answers on all 51 Qwen3-4B questions and its greedy output on 180 of 200 Qwen3-14B LongBench samples. With equal budgets on QuALITY (Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, 8B, Llama-3.1-8B) and LongHealth (three Qwen3 models), the fold is within noise of AM's accuracy in 13 of 14 settings, with lower KL to the full cache than dropping the bias in all 12 where both ran. Under the published per-head budgets, on Qwen3-4B, its Instruct-2507 variant and Llama-3.1-8B, it is within noise of AM in 9 of 10, no longer beats dropping the bias in KL, and the two each win once in accuracy.

results.title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models
results.abstract: Hybrid language models keep a key-value (KV) cache only in their few full-attention layers, but this cache is still the part of a prompt's state that grows with the prompt and that must be stored or moved to reuse it. We present DCKV, a differentiable codec for the KV cache and the first KV-cache codec that is trained end to end. Its transform, its quantizer and its entropy models, which are conditioned on the prompt tokens and on already decoded neighbouring positions, are optimized together against the frozen language model, both for the code length that the entropy models assign and for the change of the model's output. On Qwen3.5-2B, DCKV stores a compressed token in more than 55 times fewer bytes than bf16 at a loss of at most 1.8 points on three long-context benchmarks, and in more than 100 times fewer bytes at a loss of at most 3.6 points.

results.title: p-DCIM: A 28nm Probabilistic SRAM DCIM based Ising Machine for Near-Memory Context Selection in LLM-RAG Pipeline
results.abstract: We present a fabricated SRAM DCIM Ising machine that performs set-level context selection for large language model (LLM) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In RAG, the evidence-selection stage is increasingly delegated to repeated language-model reranking, which adds substantial energy to the inference pipeline. We reformulate evidence selection as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and solve it on a dual-mode digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro: the same multiply-and-accumulate datapath computes the embedding-similarity scores that populate the QUBO coefficients and evaluates the per-spin Hamiltonian differences that drive the anneal. The annealing temperature is set by a digital plane-count control along with the SRAM pseudo-read random bit flips, giving graded cooling entirely from on-chip digital configuration. The macro is taped-out in a 28 nm process [0.16 mm2, 0.41 mW] and is proposed to be integrated as part of the logic base-die in hybrid high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-bandwidth flash (HBF) stacks in a GPU package, where only the selected passage identifiers return to the host. Replacing the language-model selection pass with the near-memory Ising solver yields a macro normalized selection-energy estimate more than six orders of magnitude lower than the LLM-based baseline and reduces the evaluated total energy per query by 67%, while maintaining comparable token-level F1 on the evaluated examples.
